skill.name: find-skills
skill.description: Discovers agent skills for specific tasks, presents relevant options, and supports installation through the Skills CLI after user approval.
skill.summary: Find and evaluate installable agent skills for specialized tasks.
skill.author: brianlovin

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and public documentation links. The skill intentionally runs the Skills CLI and can globally install an unverified third-party skill while bypassing confirmation. Source review and explicit installation approval are required.

remediation.issue: The installation workflow uses global scope and disables CLI confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Remove -y, avoid global installation by default, and request explicit user approval immediately before executing the final command.

remediation.issue: Discovered third-party skills are offered for installation without source or content verification.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect the resolved repository, commit, skill contents, permissions, and security report before recommending or installing a result.

static_findings.snippet: The Skills CLI (`npx skills`) is the package manager for the open agent skills ecosystem. Skills are
- `npx skills find [query]` - Search for skills interactively or by keyword
- `npx skills add <package>` - Install a skill from GitHub or other sources
- `npx skills check` - Check for skill updates
- `npx skills update` - Update all installed skills
- User asks "how do I make my React app faster?" → `npx skills find react performance`
- User asks "can you help me with PR reviews?" → `npx skills find pr review`
- User asks "I need to create a changelog" → `npx skills find changelog`
The `-g` flag installs globally (user-level) and `-y` skips confirmation prompts.
3. **Check popular sources**: Many skills come from `vercel-labs/agent-skills` or `ComposioHQ/awesom
3. Suggest the user could create their own skill with `npx skills init`

content.value_statement: Finding the right agent extension can require broad marketplace searches and manual comparison. This skill converts a task into focused searches and presents relevant options.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the domain and specific task behind a skill request.
Builds focused keyword queries for the Skills CLI.
Runs Skills CLI searches and interprets the returned matches.
Presents skill names, purposes, installation details, and skills.sh links.
Offers installation after the user chooses a result.
Suggests direct assistance or skill creation when no match exists.
limitations: Search quality depends on the selected keywords and current marketplace index.
The workflow does not verify a skill source, contents, or security before installation.
Skills CLI and skills.sh availability affect discovery results.
Global installation changes persistent user-level agent configuration.

use_cases.title: Find Framework Guidance
use_cases.description: Search for a focused skill that improves React or Next.js performance work.

use_cases.title: Standardize Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Discover review skills that support consistent pull request checks across a team.

use_cases.title: Extend Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Compare available skills for documentation, testing, deployment, or other recurring tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Find One Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a skill that helps with React performance. Show the best match and explain its purpose. Do not install it.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants one clear recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Skill Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for pull request review skills. Compare up to three relevant options by focus, source, and expected workflow. Do not install anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user wants to compare several marketplace results.

prompt_templates.title: Search Across Related Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Find skills for end-to-end web testing. Try Playwright, browser testing, and e2e terms. Explain which result best fits a TypeScript project.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs a broader search with project context.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Before Installation
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a deployment skill for Kubernetes. Review the source and skill contents for security concerns, summarize permissions, then ask before any installation.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user requires source review and explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Find a skill for improving React application performance.
output_examples.output: Recommended match: Vercel React Best Practices. It provides React and Next.js optimization guidance. Review its skills.sh page before choosing installation.

output_examples.input: I need help reviewing pull requests.
output: A focused search found skills related to pull request review and code quality.
Each option includes its purpose, source repository, and marketplace details for comparison.

output_examples.input: Find a skill for a specialized task with no marketplace results.
output_examples.output: No relevant skill was found for the selected terms. The agent can help directly, try alternative keywords, or outline a new skill.

best_practices: Use specific task and technology keywords in each search.
Compare multiple results and review their source contents before installation.
Require explicit user approval immediately before any persistent installation.
anti_patterns: Do not install the first search result without checking its source and scope.
Do not use confirmation-bypass flags for third-party installations.
Do not treat marketplace availability as proof of security or quality.

faq.question: What does this skill search?
faq.answer: It searches the open agent skills ecosystem through the Skills CLI using keywords derived from your task.

faq.question: Can it install a selected skill?
faq.answer: Yes. Installation should occur only after source review and explicit user approval.

faq.question: Does it verify marketplace skills?
faq.answer: No. The workflow does not provide built-in security verification, reputation checks, or content auditing.

faq.question: What happens when no result matches?
faq.answer: It can try related search terms, help with the task directly, or suggest creating a new skill.

faq.question: Which agent tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does discovery require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The Skills CLI and skills.sh marketplace must be reachable for current search results and details.
